dedupe_keys.name: ribuild laboratory based investigations of the materials water activity and ph relative to mould growth

description: N.F. Jensen and colleagues at the Technical University of Denmark publish laboratory measurements from small wall assemblies with internal insulation. Temperature, relative humidity, material moisture and Mycometer results are used to investigate conditions associated with mould growth at the wall-insulation interface. The study specifically examines whether an alkaline adhesive environment can suppress growth when water activity exceeds values commonly considered critical. Photographs document preparation and experimental procedures. Zenodo lists fifteen spreadsheet, archive and document files, freely available under CC BY 4.0. The measurements support assessment of hygrothermal deterioration mechanisms in engineered building envelopes. A limitation is that the description does not give the temporal coverage, sampling intervals, material combinations or test outcomes. The thresholds named by the authors describe their study question and are not adopted here as universally safe design limits. The related historic-building survey supplies RIBuild renovation context.
